title: Advancement of Single Crystal Cathode Development via operando Scanning Electron Microscopy
content: The use of operando scanning electron microscopy (SEM) has become a powerful technique for studying Li-ion batteries [1]. It enables real-time observation of the dynamic reaction processes within the battery and its materials, facilitating the optimization of Li-ion battery performance. Among various operando methods, in-situ heating offers the unique capability to examine material structural evolution processes crucial for understanding growth mechanisms [2,3]. However, limited research has focused on the synthesis process of Li-ion battery materials. This is primarily due to the traditional heating stage’s lack of capability to introduce reaction gases into the experiment, which would better mimic the actual synthesis conditions.
